description: The bar chart illustrates a variance decomposition comparison between two LLM variants — 70B llama and 8B llama — across four domains: Health and Nutrition, Logistics, a central unlabeled category (possibly representing an aggregate or baseline), and Travel and Transportation. Each domain is represented by a pair of stacked bars, where the green segment (labeled “MVS”) and the blue segment (labeled “1-MVS”) sum to 1.0, indicating proportional contributions to total variance. In Health and Nutrition, 70B llama shows approximately 0.6 MVS and 0.4 1-MVS, while 8B llama shows 0.4 MVS and 0.6 1-MVS. In Logistics, both models show nearly equal MVS and 1-MVS (around 0.5 each). The central unlabeled category shows 70B llama with ~0.75 MVS and ~0.25 1-MVS, while 8B llama has ~0.35 MVS and ~0.65 1-MVS — the largest disparity observed. In Travel and Transportation, 70B llama has ~0.4 MVS and ~0.6 1-MVS, while 8B llama has ~0.35 MVS and ~0.65 1-MVS. The chart visually suggests that larger models (70B) tend to exhibit higher MVS (model variance share) in some domains, while smaller models (8B) show higher 1-MVS (residual or non-model variance), consistent with the paper’s focus on quantifying world model sufficiency through variance decomposition. The y-axis is scaled from 0.0 to 1.0, and the x-axis labels the model sizes under each domain. A legend at the bottom clarifies that green = MVS and blue = 1-MVS.
